After a short wait spent watching propaganda blurbs scroll past the crest of the Hegemony navy, the comm-link connects you with the office of Admiral Rao.

"So," the hero of the Siege of Raesvelg looks you over. "What's a freelancer doing at this insignificant outpost?"

The comm-link only holds briefly on the crest of the Hegemony navy before Admiral Rao appears.

"$TitleHeg," he says. "Back around Ragnar long? I hope not." The hint of a smile flickers.
He looks you over through the comm-link.

You recognize Rao's expression - the stoic face of a commanding officer who is disappointed - but more than that, angry - with a subordinate who has risked the mission through not only ignorance but poor fundamental judgment and character.

"$TitleHeg. You mingled with a Persean League spy. And then come to me to pour his lies on my desk?"

You recognize Rao's expression - the stoic, blank face of a commanding officer who is truly angry with a subordinate who has risked the mission through more than ignorance but poor fundamental judgment and character.

"$TitlePL." His voice is controlled. "I extent great leeway by even accepting your comms request. Then you pour the lies of a League spy on my desk."

You recognize Rao's expression - the stoic face of a commanding officer who is disappointed - but more than that, angry - with a civilian who has risked the mission through not only ignorance but poor fundamental judgment and character.

"Captain. You've mingled with a Persean League spy. Then come to me and you pour his lies onto my desk."
He takes a slow breath, eyes fixed on your through the link.
"That's a luxury we have not been able to afford for a long, long time, $titleHeg," he says, almost a growl.
"Then you'll be looking for a long time, $titlePL," he says, almost a growl.
"Keep looking, spacer," he says, almost a growl.
"Correct," he says, almost a growl.
"Your condescension is unwelcome, spacer," he says, almost a growl.

"This conversation is over."

The link cuts.

* * *

It might be wise to wait a day or so before trying to contact Admiral Rao again."

He blows some air out through his nostrils, barely a laugh.

"Trading tired banter with you, it appears." He makes a show of checking a secondary display. For the time, perhaps.

"I am busy, if you can believe it. Perhaps you had something useful, or at least interesting to say?"

"No." His amused tone grows a touch of frost.

He looks aside as he speaks. "I think not. They don't give medals for lying in the Hegemony..."

Then he holds a finger to his lips, thoughtfully. "No, that's not true. Not at all. They don't give medals for lying TO the Hegemony."

He smiles again, turning back to you.

"Oh, I assure you it was a wasted gesture. Neriene Rao can handle herself- with the blade, or without."

He looks away, smiling. It quickly fades.

"Neriene was a talent. Her rebellion by way of abandoning the art..."

He looks away.

"It struck true," he says quietly, putting a hand on his chest. "Anyway, you don't need an old man like me to tell you what to think. Her mind is her own business."

"Is that so," he says, nonchalant.

"I wonder why they would have said that."

He raises an eyebrow, his affect casual.

"If I had hired this mercenary, I imagine I'd be pretty upset at how easily they gave up the identity of their employer. It's a good thing the Hegemony has an official policy forbidding the employ of mercs."

"Hmm." Rao looks you over. Is that twinkle in his eye - there are no other words for it - amusement?

"Why?"

He leaves the silence for you to fill.

"Maybe he admires my fashion sense," he says breezily.

"Speaking of interests." Rao adjusts himself in his seat, posture improving dramatically to reflect the rank of admiral which he holds.

"I'm interested in why you're having such intimate conversations with Dolos Macario."

"So you just... went along?"

He shakes his head.

Rao holds up a hand, indicating that you should stop trying to explain yourself.

"I already know the facts, $titleHeg. I'm more interested in where you stand."

He nods.

"You understand why someone in my position might view such association with the Sindrian Mutiny with a bit of skepticism, I trust. I won't belabor that point."

He leans forwards, hands together.

"I'm familiar with the facts of the matter. For the most part, $titleHeg. I'm more interested in where you stand."
He nods, though there's a wary look in his eyes.
He nods.

"We work with more than a few private-enterprise auxiliaries, shall we say. Part of my job is ensuring they've a healthy respect for the terms of their contracts."

His implication is a threat, of course. His tone, and expression, are not unfamiliar from your occasional dealings with underworld bosses.
"Good," he says distantly.
"Yes," he says. "I thought I made that pretty clear."

He leans forward.

"Now, I believe I owe you a real answer to your question. Why is Dolos Macario interested in me?"

He gives a nod, though a skeptical look remains.

"I should hope you're not simply saying that because you think it'll make me like you."

"It should be," he says with a distant look.

"Now, I believe I owe you a real answer to your question. Why is Dolos Macario interested in me?"

He leans forward.

"I suppose not," he says. "Though the Hegemony bureaucracy might believe otherwise."

"Now, I believe I owe you a real answer to your question. Why is Dolos Macario interested in me?"

He leans forward.

"No, it doesn't hurt," he says, amused. 

His look grows distant for a moment. "I've discovered that with high connections you can find forgiveness in unexpected places." He shakes his head.

"Now, I believe I owe you a real answer to your question. Why is Dolos Macario interested in me?"

He leans forward.
He raises an eyebrow. "You think a lone spacer can bring down the Sindrian Diktat?"

He laughs.

"Well, I suppose I owe a real answer to your question. Why is Macario interested in me?"

He leans forward.

He nods.

"I suppose I owe a real answer to your question. Why is Macario interested in me?"

He leans forward.

"Really?" He looks legitimately perplexed. "An outsider with no connection to the ruling clique or official ideology swoops in and claims executive control based on... what, force alone?"

Rao taps his chin, considering.

"I see where you got the idea. But warfleets aside, you do lack connections with the local elite. And you've not benefited from twenty cycles of the Hegemony propaganda machine building you up as the savior of human civilization itself."

"So no." He shakes his head. "I don't think so."

"If you were lucky you could be another Loke or Leonis. But they never built anything, they only destroyed. And how they died?"

Rao gives you a look- is that how you want to end up?
"Then you will receive no answer in return," he says. "Now don't try to ask again, I don't abide a pest."

"Because I am going to destroy the Sindrian Mutiny, and him with it."

Rao puts his hands together, fingers interlaced.

"Anything else?"

"You have promise, captain, that's true. But," he takes on an avuncular tone, "I don't think you've got enough experience to handle what I've got in mind."

"Put yourself out there, take on some jobs. We may speak again on this later."

His tone makes it clear that the issue is settled. For now.

"You have promise, captain. Especially if your captaining is anything like your swordplay. You spilled blood for honor in personal combat. That is more than most can say."

He pauses. "It speaks well for you, for what I have in mind."

"You have promise, captain. You were brave enough to take up the sword with full knowledge of the art, fight... and lose. Your blood was spilled for honor in personal combat. That is more than most can say."

He pauses. "It speaks well for you, for what I have in mind."

"The truth makes few friends." Rao produces a wry smile.

"I never could stand a fool, especially when that fool is an honorable member of the Strategic Assembly. So," he holds his hand out to indicate his surroundings, Ragnar Complex.

"It's not so bad."

"A proper officer of the Hegemony is taught to leap toward the enemy, blazing guns. Once the noise quiets down, they'll wait, slack-jawed, for the medals to be pinned to their uniforms." 

"Such is the way of the Domain, which we must uphold."

He half-raises a finger, a quirk on his lips. "Officially," he concludes.

"Baikal was kind enough to find me a place where I could get important work done. I deal with... let us call them 'unique circumstances'. And for this I find it necessary to associate with energetic freelancers."

"I'll ensure you're paid promptly for a roster of small merc jobs."

"Then, perhaps something big will come up. When it does, I want to know I can count on you."

"I'm offering you the chance to be the grit that throws history off its axis."

He lets his sly smile fade. "There are many bodies of power turning just now. Grinding away, warships and bombings and riots and resources."

"The Persean Sector needs change, or it will grind what's left of us to dust."
"Good," his approval comes with his sly smile. "Have your people set up secure comms. We'll show the Strategic Assembly how it's done."

He turns a fearsome look upon you and holds it for a moment.

Then laughs at your insolence.

"It's true," he says with a slight smile. "However distantly. It is a name that comes with a great deal of... undeclared cargo, let us say."

"I am, however, my own man." Bellamy shrugs. "And I expect anyone of good manners will respect this, and not be so thick-headed as to ask if I am part of her organization. Because I am not."

He fixes you with a look, however indulgent, that makes it clear that this line of inquiry may be considered finished.
